summary: Reviewed 23 files (20 modified API method classes, 1 new test file, 2 PHPUnit configs). Systematic OWASP Top 10 review complete. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium finding (access-control gap in SetMailingStateAPI finalization path — does not block). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 — Broken Access Control (Medium): SetMailingStateAPI missing RIGHT_FINALIZE_MAILS Tier 2 check. File: assets/classes/Maileditor/Mails/API/Methods/SetMailingStateAPI.php. The WP-005 plan note states 'the finalization-specific right (RIGHT_FINALIZE_MAILS) is a Tier 2 concern checked in collectRequestData(), not the gate.' However, no check for MailRightsInterface::RIGHT_FINALIZE_MAILS ('PublishMails') exists anywhere in SetMailingStateAPI.php — not in collectResponseData(), setMailingState(), handleFinalize(), or any helper method. Any API key pseudo-user holding RIGHT_EDIT_MAILS can trigger the draft→finalized (publish) transition without the PublishMails right. Severity is Medium (not High) because: (1) the user must already hold a valid API key and RIGHT_EDIT_MAILS; (2) the authorize() gate still fires; (3) the gap is a privilege over-extension within existing authorized users. Remediation: Add a hasRight(MailRightsInterface::RIGHT_FINALIZE_MAILS) check at the start of handleFinalize() and send a 403 ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RIGHTS response if the check fails. This is consistent with the plan's stated two-tier model. Note: this gap pre-exists WP-005 — WP-005 did not introduce it; it only added the Tier 1 gate. Flagged for a follow-up work package.

A01 — Privilege-mapping review (Info): QA handoff asked to verify right assignments are minimally-sufficient. DeleteComtypeVariableAPI and DeleteValueVariationAPI are assigned RIGHT_DELETE_COMTYPES (not RIGHT_EDIT_COMTYPES). This means a user with edit-but-not-delete rights cannot remove comtype sub-entities (variables, value variations). This is a restrictive policy choice, not an over-privilege issue. Policy is consistent with the plan's mapping table. No action required unless the business rule is revisited.

A01 — Authorization gate ordering confirmed correct: authorize() is called after validate() but before collectResponseData() in BaseAPIMethod._process(). The method-whitelist check runs before the right check. API key null-guard in authorize() is safe because validate() rejects requests with a missing required apiKey parameter before authorize() is reached.

A08 — Software Integrity: All 20 getRequiredRight() overrides carry the #[Override] attribute (PHP 8.3+). If APIKeyMethodInterface or APIKeyMethodTrait signature changes, PHP will raise an error at class load time, preventing silent drift. Consistent and appropriate use.

A09 — Logging: Authorization failures log via $this->log('API authorization failed: pseudo-user lacks the required right.') in BaseAPIMethod.authorize(). Audit trail for rights-gate rejections is present.

Read-only methods (GetComtypesAPI, GetComtypeAPI, GetMailingsAPI, GetMailingAPI, ValidateMailAPI, ValidateMailAudienceAPI, GetMailExportBatchAPI, etc.) correctly do not implement APIKeyMethodInterface and are therefore not subject to the rights gate. No missing right declarations on read-only paths.

summary: WP-005 PASS with Fix-Forward. All 20 getRequiredRight() overrides are correctly implemented, use #[Override], and map to the right constants per the plan's mapping table. GetRequiredRightTest follows the MailTestCase pattern and covers all 20 methods via PHPUnit 13 DataProvider. phpunit.xml and phpunit-unit.xml both register the api-methods suite. PHPStan: 3907 files, 0 errors. Single-right-per-method gate pattern is consistent with every other API method class in the codebase.

Fix-Forward applied: CreateMailAPI.php and CreateMailAudienceAPI.php both pre-dated the #[Override] convention and WP-005 added only getRequiredRight() with the attribute, leaving all other overrides bare. Applied #[Override] to getMethodName(), getVersions(), getCurrentVersion(), init(), collectRequestData(), collectResponseData(), getDescription(), getChangelog(), getRelatedMethodNames(), getExampleJSONResponse(), getResponseKeyDescriptions(), and getGroup() in both files. PHPStan validates all placements are correct (0 errors). Tests unchanged: 20/20 pass, 61 assertions.

Security Auditor's three review points confirmed: (1) single-right-per-method gate pattern is consistent with existing API method classes; (2) #[Override] usage is now correct and consistent across all 22 affected files; (3) GetRequiredRightTest.php follows the MailTestCase base class pattern correctly.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied to CreateMailAPI.php: Added #[Override] to the 12 pre-existing override methods that were bare before WP-005: getMethodName(), getVersions(), getCurrentVersion(), init(), collectRequestData(), collectResponseData(), getDescription(), getChangelog(), getRelatedMethodNames(), getExampleJSONResponse(), getResponseKeyDescriptions(), getGroup(). WP-005 added only getRequiredRight() with the attribute, making those methods visibly inconsistent. The fix is non-behavioral; PHPStan validated all placements (3907 files, 0 errors), all 20 tests continue to pass.

Fix-Forward applied to CreateMailAudienceAPI.php: Added #[Override] to the same 12 pre-existing override methods: getMethodName(), getVersions(), getCurrentVersion(), init(), collectRequestData(), collectResponseData(), getDescription(), getChangelog(), getRelatedMethodNames(), getExampleJSONResponse(), getResponseKeyDescriptions(), getGroup(). Same rationale as CreateMailAPI.php above.

Architecture note: The two-tier rights model (Tier 1 gate via getRequiredRight() in authorize(); Tier 2 fine-grained check in collectResponseData()) is a sound and extensible design. The SetMailingStateAPI finalization gap (missing RIGHT_FINALIZE_MAILS check on the draft→finalized path) is a pre-existing Tier 2 issue correctly flagged by the Security Auditor for a follow-up WP. The current WP-005 scope is complete and correct.

Test design: The data-provider approach in GetRequiredRightTest.php is well-suited for long-term maintainability. Adding a new APIKeyMethodInterface implementor only requires one new entry in the corresponding provider array. The real-class instantiation pattern (new $className(APIManager::getInstance())) validates the #[Override] attribute at runtime, not just statically — a stronger guarantee than a mock-based approach.
